faqs.question: When is Propose Day 2027?
faqs.answer: Propose Day 2027 is Monday 8 February. It is the second day of Valentine week, which opens with Rose Day on Sunday 7 February and closes with Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February. In 2026 the day fell on a Sunday, so 2027 is a working Monday for most people.

faqs.question: Should I write to my girlfriend as तुम, तू or आप?
faqs.answer: तुम in almost every case — it is the familiar pronoun between partners. तू only if you already use it with her and with nobody else, and आप only if that is genuinely how the two of you speak. Switching for the occasion is the clearest sign a line was copied.

faqs.question: Do these Hindi lines change if the sender is a woman?
faqs.answer: No. Every published line here was chosen so that no first-person verb carries sender gender, so the same form works whoever is typing. Agreement for the person being addressed is feminine throughout, which is what makes them girlfriend lines.

faqs.question: Is it a bad idea to send her a line from a Hindi film?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and for two reasons. Film dialogue and lyrics are copyrighted, and film romance is a written screen register — a 2013 study of Raj Kapoor's early films describes its love dialogues as stagey and stilted, with the real feeling carried by song and imagery instead.

faqs.question: Can I send these in Roman Hindi instead of Devanagari?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every line on this page carries a Roman transliteration under the Devanagari, so you can paste either. Send the Devanagari if she reads it — it looks written rather than typed out phonetically.

faqs.question: What is the difference between propose day wishes, quotes and shayari for a girlfriend?
faqs.answer: A wish is addressed and sent to one person. A quote is a quotable line with no addressee, which is why it reads as a caption. Shayari is a poetic form with metre, and on this page it is the thing being deliberately declined.

faqs.question: How were the Hindi lines on this page checked?
faqs.answer: Every content word was looked up in McGregor's Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary and every inflected form was checked against two Hindi corpora — the Universal Dependencies Hindi HDTB treebank and the Tatoeba Hindi sentence set. Nine drafted lines were cut rather than published unverified.

faqs.question: Is गर्लफ्रेंड the right word to use in a Hindi message?
faqs.answer: It is an English loan written in Devanagari, and that is how it is normally written and said in Hindi conversation. There is no neutral native equivalent that carries the same meaning, so the loan is the honest choice rather than a formal substitute nobody uses.

faqs.question: What should I send if I am actually asking her out on 8 February 2027?
faqs.answer: Ask in person if you can that week; a message is the weakest form of a real question. If you cannot, a built page carries the ask better than a chat line — 91.2% of pages started on SubhSandesh are published and shared (4,615 of 5,061, platform-wide).

faqs.question: Are the SubhSandesh templates available in Hindi?
faqs.answer: No. The templates are English-language, so the built-in labels and buttons are in English. Whatever you type into the fields can be Devanagari or Roman Hindi, but if you want the whole page to read in Hindi, a typed message does that and a template does not.

faqs.question: How many of these lines should I send at once?
faqs.answer: One. Two lines from the same group compete with each other, and a block of copied lines reads as a forward rather than a message. Pick the group that matches what you are actually doing and send only that line.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Wishes for Girlfriend in Hindi, Not Film Dialogue

Propose Day 2027 falls on **Monday 8 February**, the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February and before Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February. The ten Hindi lines below are for one recipient — a girlfriend — and all ten avoid the register most Hindi romance has been performed at you in: film register. Each carries Devanagari, a Roman transliteration, an English gloss and its pronoun marked तुम, तू or आप.

SubhSandesh has 5,061 personalised pages created since 12 March 2026 across 20 page types, platform-wide, and 38.7% of those creators password-protect a page before sharing (1,961 of 5,061, platform-wide) — an instinct nobody applies to a copied caption.

## What a Propose Day wish for a girlfriend in Hindi actually is

A Propose Day wish for a girlfriend in Hindi is a short line in Devanagari, sent on 8 February to one person you are with or about to ask. It is correspondence, not a caption, and it has one reader.

That single reader is the difference from a quote list. A quote works on anybody; a wish has to survive someone who knows how you talk.

Sending to a wife, a friend or a family group instead? The routing page is [Propose Day wishes in Hindi by recipient](/blog/propose-day-wishes-in-hindi). This page does the girlfriend case only.

## Why film Hindi is the wrong register to send her

Most Hindi speakers have watched romance conducted almost entirely on screen, and that version is a written, heightened idiom, not conversation. Rachel Dwyer's 2013 study of Raj Kapoor's early films argues that his blend of romance, sexuality and spirituality [created a language for the expression of emotion](https://www.southasianist.ed.ac.uk/southasianist/article/view/697) — built for the screen, by professionals.

She is specific about where it falls down. Reading *Aag* (1948), she records dialogues about love and its passions that "feel very stagey and stilted", with the expression of emotionality sitting less in the dialogue than in imagery of fire and water, and in song.

Cinema moves the real feeling into the song. Srijana Siri Murthy's 2023 reading of *Pyaasa* (1957) notes that Hindi-film characters [sing the vocals diegetically](https://cinej.pitt.edu/ojs/cinej/article/view/421), unlike Hollywood's background scoring, each song working as a poem conveying the protagonist's emotional state.

So the inherited model is: feeling is versed and sung, plain speech is the stagey part. Paste that into a message and you have sent a performance.

The loudest current version is worse to borrow. A 2026 study of Sandeep Reddy Vanga's *Kabir Singh* (2019) and *Animal* (2023) finds both films [romanticize dominance and aggression](https://cinej.pitt.edu/ojs/cinej/article/view/806) as integral to passionate love.

Film register travels back into ordinary speech, which is why it reads as borrowed. Max Kramer's 2014 Heidelberg working paper follows [Tapori Hindi out into everyday language attitudes and back](https://fid4sa-repository.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/3157/), through a stock Bombay figure whose performance pushes registers to their margins.

## 10 Propose Day wishes in Hindi for a girlfriend, grouped by what you are saying

All ten were written for this page. None is a film line or song lyric, and none carries a first-person verb that changes with the sender's gender, so one form works whoever types it. Agreement for the person addressed is feminine throughout.

### 1. Say the one true sentence (तुम)

> **मुझे तुमसे प्यार है। आज कहने का बहाना मिल गया।**
> *Mujhe tumse pyaar hai. Aaj kahne ka bahaana mil gaya.*
> I love you. Today I got an excuse to say it.

> **कोई शायरी नहीं, बस सीधी बात: मुझे तुमसे प्यार है।**
> *Koi shaayari nahin, bas seedhi baat: mujhe tumse pyaar hai.*
> No shayari, just the plain thing: I love you.

Register: तुम, the familiar pronoun between partners.
Who it suits: anyone saying it for the first time, or the hundredth.
When not to send it: never both. The second works only alone.

### 2. Name one specific thing (तुम)

> **तुम्हारे साथ मेरा दिन आसान हो जाता है।**
> *Tumhaare saath mera din aasaan ho jaata hai.*
> My day gets easier with you.

> **तुम्हारे साथ मुझे कुछ बनना नहीं पड़ता।**
> *Tumhaare saath mujhe kuchh banna nahin padta.*
> With you I do not have to become anything.

Register: तुम.
Who it suits: a relationship past the first months, where a general declaration reads as automatic.
When not to send it: if it is not true that day. Specific claims are checkable, which is why they land.

### 3. Ask, do not announce (तुम)

> **एक सीधा सवाल: क्या तुम मेरी गर्लफ्रेंड बनोगी?**
> *Ek seedha sawaal: kya tum meri girlfriend banogi?*
> One plain question: will you be my girlfriend?

> **दो साल हो गए, और सवाल आज भी वही है: तुम मेरे साथ रहोगी?**
> *Do saal ho gaye, aur sawaal aaj bhi wahi hai: tum mere saath rahogi?*
> Two years on, and the question is still the same: will you stay with me?

Register: तुम. गर्लफ्रेंड is an English loan, normally written in Devanagari like this.
Who it suits: line one for a real ask on 8 February; line two for a couple already together.
When not to send it: not by message, if you can ask in person that week.

### 4. Thank her instead of declaring (तुम)

> **तुमने उस दिन हाँ कहा था। आज उसके लिए शुक्रिया।**
> *Tumne us din haan kaha tha. Aaj uske liye shukriya.*
> You said yes that day. Thank you for it today.

> **तुम्हारे साथ बात करना अच्छा लगता है।**
> *Tumhaare saath baat karna achha lagta hai.*
> I like talking with you.

Register: तुम.
Who it suits: anyone whose relationship is old enough that a declaration is not news.
When not to send it: not after a bigger message. Gratitude reads best alone.

### 5. If you already speak to her as आप (आप)

> **आपसे बात किए बिना दिन पूरा नहीं लगता।**
> *Aapse baat kiye bina din poora nahin lagta.*
> The day does not feel complete without talking to you.

Register: आप, the respectful pronoun.
Who it suits: couples who genuinely use आप with each other, commoner in some families than the internet suggests.
When not to send it: if you normally say तुम. Switching pronoun for the occasion is the clearest sign of a copied line.

### 6. If तू is already yours (तू)

> **तू साथ है तो सब आसान है।**
> *Tu saath hai to sab aasaan hai.*
> If you are there, everything is easy.

Register: तू, the intimate pronoun.
Who it suits: couples who already use तू with each other and nobody else.
When not to send it: anywhere it is not established. तू is warm inside a close pair and reads as contempt outside one.

## तुम, तू or आप — use the pronoun you already use

Hindi makes you choose a second-person pronoun before you can inflect a verb, so the choice is unavoidable and it encodes the relationship. तू is intimate, तुम the familiar default between partners, आप respectful.

For a girlfriend, तुम is right in almost every case. The test is not which pronoun sounds romantic; it is which one you used in your last ten messages.

Every content word above was checked against McGregor's *Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary* and every inflected form against two Hindi corpora. 9 of 19 drafted lines were cut, one because a verb form could not be confirmed.

## Which line fits which moment

Five situations, the pronoun each takes, how to send it. Every figure in the last column is SubhSandesh's own, platform-wide across 20 page types.

| What you are doing | Pronoun | How to send it | Platform-wide SubhSandesh signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Asking her for the first time | तुम | In person if possible; a built page if not | 91.2% of started pages are published and shared (4,615 of 5,061) |
| Saying it again, years in | तुम | Typed in your existing thread | 38.7% password-protect before sharing (1,961 of 5,061) |
| Marking the day, nothing more | तुम | One line, no image, no forward | 48.4% of views are on a phone (27,185 of 56,152) |
| Writing to a partner who uses आप | आप | Typed, matching her pronoun | 11.1 average views per created page |
| Sending while apart | तू or तुम | A link she can open on a phone | 56,152 recorded views of shared pages |

Read row two against row three: where four in ten creators lock a page before sending it, a forwarded caption is the opposite instinct.

## Where a SubhSandesh page helps, and where it cannot

For a real ask on 8 February, a chat line is the weakest form of the question. The [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) walks your story and ends on a YES button that grows every time she dodges it.

For a girlfriend that is usually still the wrong template: "will you marry me" is a different question. The honest fit is the [I love you page](/love-gf) — second most-created page type at 1,173 pages, 23.2% of everything built, and most-viewed at 16,902 views, 30.1% of all page views, both platform-wide.

The limit that matters here: the templates are English-language. A Hindi reader gets the animation, photos, music, structure, and whatever Hindi **you** type into the fields in Devanagari or Roman — but the labels and buttons around your words are English. For a page that reads wholly in Hindi, a typed message does it and a template does not.

[Browse the template list](/templates) only after you know which question you are asking.

A page is wrong outright for the smallest version of this. If the true message is one sentence, send one sentence. Nearly half of all views on shared pages happen on a phone — 48.4%, 27,185 of 56,152, platform-wide — so a designed page on a slow connection delivers a worse evening than one line of Devanagari.

No figure here is proposal-specific: a read-only probe of that collection is refused by this machine's production-read policy, so every number is platform-wide across 20 page types or sampled on the template it names.

## Sources

- Rachel Dwyer, [Fire and Rain, The Tramp and The Trickster](https://www.southasianist.ed.ac.uk/southasianist/article/view/697), *The South Asianist* 2(3), 9–32 — 5 December 2013.
- Srijana Siri Murthy, [The Songs of Pyaasa: A Narrative within a Narrative](https://cinej.pitt.edu/ojs/cinej/article/view/421), *CINEJ Cinema Journal* 11(1) — 19 October 2023.
- Singh, Pathak and Mishra, [Examining Toxic Masculinity under the Guise of 'Romance' in Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Hindi Films](https://cinej.pitt.edu/ojs/cinej/article/view/806), *CINEJ Cinema Journal* 14(1) — 22 May 2026.
- Max Kramer, [Sprachliche Imagination im Film: Tapori Hindi](https://fid4sa-repository.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/3157/), Working Papers in Modern South Asian Languages and Literatures 2, Heidelberg — 10 March 2014. Abstract read only.

structuralLimitations: The Hindi lines were NOT reviewed by a native speaker. They were verified instrumentally: every content word against McGregor's Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary via the Digital Dictionaries of South Asia headword query, and every inflected form against two corpora — the Universal Dependencies Hindi HDTB treebank (train+dev+test, indexed locally to 19,088 distinct surface forms) and the Tatoeba Hindi sentence export (16,475 sentences). Instrumental verification is not native review and does not replace it.

One published form is composed rather than directly attested: बनोगी in “क्या तुम मेरी गर्लफ्रेंड बनोगी?” appears 0 times in either corpus. It is paradigm-regular: बनोगे is attested for this exact stem (“तुम क्या बनोगे?”) and the feminine -ोगी ending is attested on six other verbs (करोगी, चाहोगी, पहनोगी, कहोगी, गिरोगी, तैरोगी). Every other published form is directly attested, including रहोगी in exactly this frame (“तुम मेरे साथ रहोगी।”).

19 Hindi lines were drafted and 9 cut. Three cuts were verification failures: हँसती occurs 0 times in either corpus (only हँसना once and हँसते twice); ख़ास could not be resolved in McGregor at all because the nukta form breaks the DSAL query interface and the un-nukta'd headword खास is attested only as “f. reg. (W.) a square-cut bag; a load, bagful”, a different word; and अच्छी दोस्त with feminine agreement occurs 0 times in either corpus while McGregor lists दोस्त as masculine. The other six were cut for register (aphoristic or rhetorical-question shapes, i.e. the film register this page argues against), for sender-gender marking, for length, and one for being too close to the wave-2 sibling's चुन रहा हूँ line.

A real finding about Hindi resources: the Universal Dependencies Hindi HDTB treebank is newswire and contains almost no second-person familiar address, so it cannot verify the register this page is written in. तुम्हें, तुमसे, आपसे, तुझे, रहोगी, बनोगी and चाहोगी are all absent from it. Tatoeba was added for exactly this reason and carries 375, 41, 23, 9, 1, 0 and 3 occurrences of those forms.

Phase 1 is inherited, not measured. No SERP was fetched for this keyword and no competitor page was read, so the post describes no competitor's content and no current ranking position. The only India-served SERPs ever captured for this territory are the 11 in content/keywords/2026-09-16-propose-100/serps.md, dated 2026-09-16, which do not include this query. Three checklist items fail for this reason and are recorded in auditReport.failed.

No proposal-specific data exists. A read-only probe of the proposalpages collection is refused by this machine's production-read policy, so every SubhSandesh figure in the body is labelled in prose as platform-wide across all 20 page types or as sampled on the named template. No number is attributed to proposal pages.
The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty, so the post states and implies no price, no free tier and no paid tier, and sidesteps the claim rather than hedging it.

Two better-fitting papers could not be read and were dropped rather than cited unread: David Lunn, “The Eloquent Language: Hindustani in 1940s Indian Cinema” (BioScope 6(1), 2015) — eprints.soas.ac.uk does not resolve from this machine (ENOTFOUND), core.ac.uk returns 410 and the green copy at soas-repository.worktribe.com returns HTTP 403; and Shalini Shankar, “Reel to real: Desi teens' linguistic engagements with Bollywood” (Pragmatics 14(2/3), 2004) — the OA PDF OpenAlex names at jbe-platform.com returns HTTP 403.

Source 4 (Kramer) is a Master's thesis in a university working-paper series, not a peer-reviewed article, and only its abstract was read; the PDF link returns an HTML terms-of-use step and the crossasia-repository address OpenAlex prefers does not resolve from this machine. The post does not present it as peer-reviewed. The other three sources are peer-reviewed, open access and were read in full.

They were deliberately kept out of batchMeta.sources throughout and are disclosed here and in the research brief instead; listing them would have pushed two domains to 4 and hard-failed the batch verifier.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page on this keyword that treats the reader's problem as a register problem — that the Hindi he has heard romance conducted in is screen Hindi, stagey in dialogue by Dwyer's own reading of Aag and with the feeling displaced into song by Murthy's reading of Pyaasa — and then publishes lines chosen against that standard rather than in imitation of it. Three things here are not available to a competitor: the film-studies grounding, the verification trail (McGregor plus two corpora, 19 drafted, 9 cut, each cut with a stated reason), and SubhSandesh's platform-wide behaviour. Realistic target is position 6–10, not 3: this is a February news cycle owned by national Hindi newsrooms whose domain authority and refresh cadence this domain cannot match. It is also a copy-text query with near-zero conversion — the searcher copies a line and leaves — so judge the page on impressions, not on signups, and do not expect it to convert. Its remaining risk is cannibalisation: the wave-2 page propose-day-wishes-in-hindi is on the same category and the same festival, and Google may cluster them; the mitigation is a one-way contextual link to it as the routing page for every other recipient, and no re-coverage of spouse, friend, sibling or group here.
